title: Essential smallness of ordinary presentable objects
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; sets and indexing categories called small belong to $\mathcal U$, and all Hom sets are small. An infinite cardinal $\eta$ is regular when a union of fewer than $\eta$ sets of cardinality less than $\eta$ has cardinality less than $\eta$. A category is $\eta$-filtered when every diagram with fewer than $\eta$ morphisms admits a cocone; for a poset this means that every subset of cardinality less than $\eta$, including the empty subset, has an upper bound. An object is $\eta$-presentable when its Hom functor preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits. Let $\eta$ be infinite regular, and let $\mathcal C$ be locally $\eta$-presentable: it has all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and a small family of $\eta$-presentable objects under whose small $\eta$-filtered colimits every object of $\mathcal C$ is obtained. Then the $\eta$-presentable objects of $\mathcal C$ form an essentially small family: there is a small set of such objects to one of which every $\eta$-presentable object is isomorphic.
